subject: Error in marprobs[leftright_nodes_matrix[, 2], ] : subscript out of bounds.

messages.author: 02762cbcbac5c01d
messages.subject: Error in marprobs[leftright_nodes_matrix[, 2], ] : subscript out of bounds.
parts:
Hi Nick, 

I have used BioGeoBEARS successfully before and have the Psychotria example working perfectly. But now, no matter what I do, when I run my own dataset even though the analysis seems to run fine and the results object looks good as far as I can tell, I keep running into this error when trying to pdf-plot the results:

Error in marprobs[leftright_nodes_matrix[, 2], ] : subscript out of bounds.

I followed some earlier advice I found regarding this error: I tried reinstalling R and upgraded to v.3.6.0, I removed all the packages and reinstalled them, and reinstalled biogeobears from the github, and also tried sourcing things directly, etc. (before the reinstallation I had a different error when plotting).

I also have confirmed all the input files several times, and don't have any 0 length branches in the tree. I tried adjusting the min/max of d, e, and j to 0.00001 and 4.99999. 

Nothing seems to get rid of this error, despite the Psychotria example working and plotting correctly each time. I just get the error when trying to plot any of my own analyses (DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE).

Any advice would be very much appreciated!

I can send the input files offline if that would be helpful.

-Ben

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Error in marprobs[leftright_nodes_matrix[, 2], ] : subscript out of bounds.
parts:
Hi -- it runs fine for me, the key was that the plotting part of the example script assumes you have your tree loaded in "tr" and your geography data loaded in "tipranges".  These preliminary steps had been cut from the top of your script, so probably your analysis was trying to plot on some other "tr" object you had loaded which didn't match.

It worked after I added this near the top:

============
trfn = np(paste(wd, "Draco_UltraTree_MLtopov2.txt", sep="/"))      # Newick tree file

# NJM:
tr=read.tree(trfn)

geogfn = np(paste(wd, "Draco_Areas_12.txt", sep="/"))            # Geography areas file

# NJM:
# Look at your geographic range data:
tipranges = getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geogfn)
tipranges

# Maximum range size observed:
max(rowSums(dfnums_to_numeric(tipranges@df)))
============

Cheers!
Nick
